title: Throughput escrow and graceful swarm replacement for compacted maintenance windows
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets experience efficiency loss and SLO jitter during back-to-back maintenance windows when multiple nodes are drained in compacted intervals. Existing drain workflows cause sudden throughput cliffs and require conservative overprovisioning. We need an operational pattern that lets us compact maintenance events (fewer, denser windows) without exposing customers to tail latency spikes or sustained unit-cost inflation.

Proposed solution: Introduce a throughput escrow abstraction and a "graceful swarm replacement" workflow. Throughput escrow lets the maintenance orchestration temporarily 'lock' an amount of throughput capacity from the fleet as a tokenized reservation (an escrow) that auto-fills from warm standby hosts or transient burst capacity. The graceful swarm replacement coordinates staggered drains inside a compacted window by: 1) allocating escrows per maintenance shard, 2) prewarming KV caches for escrowed capacity using predictive traffic replays, 3) progressively diverting traffic to escrowed hosts while draining origin hosts, and 4) returning escrowed capacity after KV-warm handoff completed.

Key behaviors: 
- Escrow tokens are assigned at the host-pool level and visible to autoscaler and routing layers.
- Escrow capacity is time-boxed and backed by a cost-accounting ledger so billing/SLAs remain auditable.
- Autoscaler integration: escrows signal hedging demand to the autoscaler to spin short-lived burst instances when warm standby is insufficient.
- Safety: if prewarm fails or latency increases above threshold, the orchestration pauses the drain and triggers rollback to origin host.

Why different from current drain orchestration: this approach pairs a tokenized reservation with active prewarm + traffic replay (instead of blind staggered drains), and it treats compacted maintenance as a first-class operation with economic accounting (escrow ledger) and autoscaler hedging to avoid conservative overprovisioning.

Success metrics (targets):
- 90th percentile tail latency delta during compacted maintenance <= +5% relative to steady-state
- Average extra GPU-minutes consumed for hedging <= 7% over baseline for typical windows
- Rollback events < 1 per 100 maintenance shards in canary rollout

Scope: prototype orchestration + escrow API, autoscaler hook, KV prewarm job, traffic router changes, and a simulation harness for canary validation.

Deliverables: 
- API: /fleet/escrows (create/read/cancel) + ledger events
- Orchestrator: graceful-swarm-replacement state machine implementation in maintenance service
- Autoscaler: hedging signal handler + short-lived instance profile
- Prewarm: predictive KV prewarm job that can replay sampled traffic from observability traces
- Simulation: synthetic traffic runner to validate SLOs under compacted windows

Dependencies: autoscaler team (ENG-149999), router/traffic-split team (ENG-141010), KV-cache team (ENG-132211).

Rollout plan: develop feature-flagged prototype -> internal canary on a small dedicated pool with low-customer-impact tags -> expand to dedicated staging fleets -> default-on for compacted maintenance windows after 3 successful cycles and metrics green.

Security & compliance: escrow ledger events must be exportable to audit logs; KMS keys used for any token signing (security review required).
